Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.text: They brought forth the he goats for the sin offering, and the priests killed them, and they made reconciliation with their blood upon the altar, to make an atonement for all Israel, for the king commanded the burnt offering and the sin offering for all Israel. All twelve, because Hezekiah was bringing them back together, with the strangers who showed up for Passover. Reconciliation and atonement were through animals, and Christ's body replaced them; atonement, reconciliation, and justification are three words for the same thing, for the same people, with the same God.
precepts.point: And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement, the margin says reconciliation. Reconcile in verse 10 and atonement in verse 11 are the same word: Christ died and brought us back to the Father, which is also called adoption. Christianity starts Romans 5 in the middle where it is confusing; start earlier and it is clear.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
In the days of Hezekiah, “they brought forth the he goats for the sin offering before the king and the congregation; and they laid their hands upon them: And the priests killed them, and they made reconciliation with their blood upon the altar, to make an atonement for all Israel: for the king commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering should be made for all Israel.”

All means all twelve, because Hezekiah was trying to bring them back together: all twelve tribes, and the strangers that showed up for the Passover.

Here reconciliation and atonement stand side by side, and they were made through the blood of animals. When Christ died, his body replaced them. That is why Romans 5:9 says “being now justified by his blood”: his blood replaces the animals, the works we no longer receive justification from. And the time came, as Daniel 9 foretold, when the temple was destroyed, the priests scattered abroad and not one stone left standing. With no way left to atone with animals, we had to have faith in Christ; otherwise you condemn yourself, indebted to a law you can no longer keep.

So atonement, reconciliation and justification are three words for the same thing, for the same people, with the same God. Reconciliation is the restoration of a friendly relationship, a reuniting; you cannot reunite with someone you were never joined to. Israel was with God before, rebelled until “he was turned to be their enemy”, and through the death of his Son was brought back again. That is Romans 5:10: “when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son”.

precepts.text: The oil for the lamps and the showbread were commanded to be kept continually, an everlasting statute the fathers had abandoned.
precepts.point: He names the sin plainly: the fathers had trespassed, forsaken the Most High, turned their backs on his habitation, shut the doors, put out the lamps, and stopped burning incense and offering burnt offerings.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 29: Hezekiah Cleanses the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
The Most High commanded “pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually”, “a statute for ever in your generations.” Aaron was to “order the lamps upon the pure candlestick before the Lord continually.” The twelve cakes of the showbread were set “in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the Lord”, with “pure frankincense upon each row”, and “Every sabbath he shall set it in order before the Lord continually, being taken from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant.”

The oil for the lamps and the showbread were to be kept continually, an everlasting statute, and the fathers abandoned it. Hezekiah names the sin plainly: “they have shut up the doors of the porch, and put out the lamps, and have not burned incense nor offered burnt offerings in the holy place unto the God of Israel.” They “have forsaken him, and have turned away their faces from the habitation of the Lord, and turned their backs.”

So Hezekiah, who “did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father had done”, went straight to it: “in the first year of his reign, in the first month”, he “opened the doors of the house of the Lord, and repaired them”, and charged the Levites, “sanctify now yourselves, and sanctify the house of the Lord God of your fathers, and carry forth the filthiness out of the holy place.”

precepts.text: If Israel turns from the commandments, the Most High will cast the house out of his sight and make Israel a proverb and a byword among all people.
precepts.point: The same warning was spoken over Solomon: turning from the commandments would make Israel a proverb and a byword, an astonishment to all who passed by. That is exactly how the nations look at scattered Israel today.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 29: Hezekiah Cleanses the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
The same warning was spoken over Solomon: “if ye shall at all turn from following me, ye or your children, and will not keep my commandments and my statutes”, “Then will I cut off Israel out of the land which I have given them; and this house, which I have hallowed for my name, will I cast out of my sight; and Israel shall be a proverb and a byword among all people”.

At this house “every one that passeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss”, and they will ask why. The answer: “Because they forsook the Lord their God, who brought forth their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and have taken hold upon other gods”.

Hezekiah saw it come to pass: “the wrath of the Lord was upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he hath delivered them to trouble, to astonishment, and to hissing, as ye see with your eyes.” And, “our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives are in captivity for this.” That is exactly how the nations look at scattered Israel today: a proverb and a byword, an astonishment to all who pass by.

precepts.text: If when we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more being reconciled we shall be saved by his life.
precepts.point: Under the law, atonement required animal sacrifice, but the reconciliation the Most High provides now is through the death of his son. You cannot be reconciled to someone you were never joined to, so the reconciliation is for the house of Israel his people.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 29: Hezekiah Cleanses the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
“For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.”

Under the law, atonement required animal sacrifice. Hezekiah brought “seven bullocks, and seven rams, and seven lambs, and seven he goats, for a sin offering for the kingdom, and for the sanctuary, and for Judah.” The priests sprinkled the blood upon the altar, “and they made reconciliation with their blood upon the altar, to make an atonement for all Israel”.

But the reconciliation the Most High provides now is through the death of his Son. And you cannot be reconciled to someone you were never joined to, so the reconciliation is for the house of Israel, his people, just as Hezekiah’s offering was made “for all Israel.”

precepts.text: The singers among the Levites were employed in that work day and night, showing the ordained pattern of temple music Hezekiah restored.
precepts.point: The king and princes command the Levites to sing praise with the words of David and Asaph the seer, and they sing with gladness and bow their heads in worship.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 29: Hezekiah Cleanses the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
“And these are the singers, chief of the fathers of the Levites, who remaining in the chambers were free: for they were employed in that work day and night.” The singers among the Levites were employed in that work day and night. That is the ordained pattern of temple music, and Hezekiah restored it.

He “set the Levites in the house of the Lord with cymbals, with psalteries, and with harps, according to the commandment of David, and of Gad the king’s seer, and Nathan the prophet”. And “when the burnt offering began, the song of the Lord began also with the trumpets, and with the instruments ordained by David king of Israel. And all the congregation worshipped”, “until the burnt offering was finished.”

Then the king and the princes “commanded the Levites to sing praise unto the Lord with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer. And they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshipped.” The singers were back at the work they were set to.

precepts.text: Let all things be done decently and in order, the same standard by which the temple service was restored.
precepts.point: The service of the house of the Lord is set in order, and Hezekiah and the people rejoice that the thing was done suddenly, done decently and in order.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 29: Hezekiah Cleanses the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Let all things be done decently and in order.” That is the same standard by which the temple service was restored.

Once the people were consecrated, they brought so many sacrifices and thank offerings that “the priests were too few, so that they could not flay all the burnt offerings: wherefore their brethren the Levites did help them, till the work was ended”, “for the Levites were more upright in heart to sanctify themselves than the priests.” Everyone took his place, and the burnt offerings were “in abundance, with the fat of the peace offerings, and the drink offerings for every burnt offering.”

“So the service of the house of the Lord was set in order. And Hezekiah rejoiced, and all the people, that God had prepared the people: for the thing was done suddenly.” It was done suddenly, and it was done decently and in order.
